question.text: A trader sells 20 GOI bond futures contracts at a price of Rs. 97.80. Face value per contract is Rs. 2,00,000. Assuming a hypothetical initial margin of 1.5% of contract value, what is the total initial margin required?

explanation.text: The Logic: For GOI bond futures, contract value per contract = Face value x Price / 100 = 2,00,000 x 97.80 / 100 = Rs. 1,95,600. Total contract value across 20 contracts = 1,95,600 x 20 = Rs. 39,12,000. Applying the hypothetical 1.5% initial margin: 1.5% x 39,12,000 = Rs. 58,680. The Trap: Rs. 60,000 wrongly applies 1.5% to face value (1.5% of 40,00,000). Rs. 39,120 applies 1% instead of 1.5%. Rs. 78,240 applies 2% instead of 1.5%. Note: The 1.5% rate used here is hypothetical for arithmetic practice. Actual initial margin on exchange-traded interest-rate futures is determined by the clearing corporation through SPAN/VaR-based models rather than a flat percentage. T-Bill futures use a separate contract-value formula (2000 x (100 - 0.25 x y)) and are not covered by this item.
